**Solution 1 (12) is wrong.** Its claim that diamond-subdivision-free graphs have bounded clique-width fails. Diamond subdivisions are exactly the induced thetas (with at most one path of length 1), so diamond-subdivision-free means theta-free. Triangle-free theta-free graphs are $K_{2,3}$-subgraph-free, and the layered wheels of Sintiari and Trotignon are triangle-free and theta-free with unbounded treewidth. Under the Gurski–Wanke result for $K_{t,t}$-subgraph-free classes, that gives unbounded clique-width, so the diamond should not be in $\mathcal M$. Solution 1's claim that unit interval graphs kill the claw also fails, since they have bounded clique-width.

**Solution 2 (3)** requires the paw to be excluded, but none of its listed constructions kills the paw. I could not find a hereditary class of unbounded clique-width that avoids induced cycles with a pendant path. I also could not confirm that the paw survives, so I can't verify this answer either.

**Solution 3 (7)** depends on the paw surviving, and it openly leaves that step unproven. I could not settle it either way.

I can confirm that $P_4$ belongs to $\mathcal M$ (its class is the cographs), and that the diamond does not. Whether the paw belongs to $\mathcal M$, and whether any other 4-vertex graph does, is what decides between 3, 7, and other values. I could not determine this reliably, so none of the three final answers can be checked.

CHOICE: NONE
